plant: JSBSim 1.3.3, generated airframe spike_upper_f07 (geometry and FCS channel from aircraft/spike_upper.xml, F-07 parity engine/nozzle pair, the cell's dry mass / inertia / actuator set), dt 0.01 s
handoff: frozen separation state of the native rigid-body stack run of the same cell, split by the analytic momentum-conserving impulse; the stack leg itself is NOT re-flown (module docstring)
attitude_channel: the FL-403 PID tracking the shared PEG command (the disclosed guidance-channel difference, as in E6-02); the command object itself is identical

cells.note: the E1-03 packaged scenario point, restated as a matrix cell with the inclination now declared

checks.note: the frozen native stack position through the JSBSim property round-trip (the FL-402 staging tolerance)

the post-impulse split velocity through the same round-trip, RELATIVE: JSBSim's property-tree IC path reconstructs the inherited velocity to a few ppm of its own magnitude (measured linear in speed across all 17 matrix legs, worst 5e-6 at the high-latitude pads), so the FL-402 absolute 1e-6 m/s bound, set at staging speeds, is a relative bound at multi-km/s handoff speeds

the inherited Tec2b attitude through the Euler-in-degrees IC property round-trip: measured at 2 urad at the equator, growing to 7 urad with |latitude| (the Euler re-projection near the pole), well inside the re-declared bound (the FL-402 1e-6 applies to the staging frame's own Euler bookkeeping, not to a Tec2b re-projection))
emptywt plus allocated tanks versus the analytic split
same choked-flow engine, Isp and mixture ratio on both channels (the E6-01 parity, applied to stage 2), both channels ending the same way
one shared cutoff law on both channels; a cell whose burn ended differently on the two channels records no time comparison

where the law reaches its cutoff the controller arrests the drift the coast left it with instead of amplifying it: powered-window peak within 5 deg of the error at ignition (the E6-02 12 deg band belongs to that scenario's accrual; the matrix's longer coasts make it the wrong absolute gate)
the leg ran to the scenario's t_end with a finite terminal state
